evidence.finding: Same-input candidate OpProf (target timing-2, f16 8x512x3072): per-program GM_to_UB 48.375KB and UB_to_GM 48KB, but aiv_mte2_time mean 1.509us vs aiv_mte3_time 0.663us, i.e. aiv_mte2_active_bw 33.25 GB/s vs aiv_mte3_active_bw 73.66 GB/s; aiv_mte2_ratio 0.473 is the largest hardware execution lane, aiv_mte3_ratio 0.217. Equal logical bytes move at very different active rates.

Compiled tile is tensor<128x64xf16> (8192 elems). q_in rows advance by stride_qkv_s=3072 elements while columns are only 64 contiguous f16 (128B) per row; out_off uses stride_out_s=64, stride_out_d=1, so each [128,64] output store is one fully contiguous 16KB block. Load side is 128B-strided, store side contiguous - the asymmetry the profile reports.

Partial common-clock per-core window (absolute_time_qualified=false): MTE2 productive_ratio 0.701; MTE3 productive_ratio 0.153 / wait_only_ratio 0.704; VECTOR productive 0.101 / wait_only 0.649; MTE2 idle_ratio 0.299 with a 1.60us tail idle after 119.767us. Top instructions are the three strided MTE2 row loads (3.09/2.99/2.12us attributed) plus WAIT_FLAG at the q store. This keeps the load-granularity explanation alive and shows the waiting is downstream of loads, but the idle fractions are not causal proof.

Retained best c133a5a3: formal 21/21 passed, geo_mean 1.623; target timing-2 candidate 63.51us vs reference 91.14us (1.435x), and f32 timing-8 is the worst case at 1.361x. Baseline for the next measured change.

hypothesis: MTE2 is slower than MTE3 for identical logical bytes because each program reads only 64 contiguous f16 (128B) per sequence row with a 3072-element row stride, while the matching store is a fully contiguous 16KB block. If the 128B load granularity forces 512B-line fetches, neighbouring head groups re-fetch the same line in separate programs (up to 4x load waste). Grouping 4 adjacent heads into one program makes each input row a 256-element (512B) contiguous span, matching the store-side contiguity and cutting load transactions roughly 4x while keeping tile bytes, program count and all arithmetic unchanged.
alternatives: The 1.5us MTE2 time is real DRAM/L2 bandwidth saturation, in which case widening per-program load spans will not reduce it.
The cost is per-program scalar/launch overhead (aiv_scalar_ratio 0.240) rather than load granularity; halving programs, not widening loads, would be the lever.
MTE3/VECTOR waiting (wait_only 0.70/0.65) is the critical chain and loads are already overlapped, so load-side changes would be invisible.
discriminating_observation: MTE2 and MTE3 move the same 48KB per program yet MTE2 is 2.3x slower (33 vs 74 GB/s), and the compilation shows load rows are 128B-strided while stores are fully contiguous; this discriminates access granularity from pure bandwidth saturation. The scalar-share alternative predicts no MTE2/MTE3 asymmetry.
change: Rewrite the tile as [BLOCK_S, BLOCK_H, BLOCK_D] with affine h and d axes. When head_dim is an exact power of two and num_heads is divisible by the group, group BLOCK_H=4 heads (256 contiguous f16 columns = 512B rows) and shrink BLOCK_S to keep the same 16KB element budget; otherwise BLOCK_H=1 reproduces current behaviour. Input/bias/output offsets become 3D-affine; q fp32 bias+rescale, k/v fp16 adds, EXACT/masked paths and arbitrary strides are preserved. Grid decode gains num_head_groups and head0=group*BLOCK_H.
expected: aiv_mte2_time and aiv_mte2_ratio fall relative to aiv_mte3 (active load BW rises toward the ~70 GB/s store rate), per-program aiv_time decreases, and target-case task duration / formal timing-2 latency decrease. Logical bytes (GM_to_UB 48.375KB, UB_to_GM 48KB) and program count 512 stay constant; no numeric change expected (abs_err/rel_err remain 0).
validation: Preflight candidate.py; if awaiting_source_review hand off unchanged. Then paired profiling/simulator re-capture for the same timing-2 case (compare mte2/mte3 time and ratios, bytes, program count) and one formal KGS evaluation over 21 cases plus 48 supplementary checks.
layer_reason: The asymmetry is in how the tile's column span maps to global-memory bursts (input row 128B strided vs output 16KB contiguous); only the Triton tile/index mapping can widen load spans without touching host allocation, dtype, strides or arithmetic.
simulator_incremental_judgment: Hotspot analysis adds: the three strided row loads are the largest attributed MTE2 instructions, and bias loads/setup also appear as MTE2 instructions, so the load lane's instruction shape matters. Waiting/idle analysis adds: MTE3 wait_only 0.704 and VECTOR wait_only 0.649 show stores/vector spend most of the observed window waiting on upstream data, and MTE2 has a 1.6us tail idle, which is consistent with a load-latency chain, but the partial window (absolute_time_qualified=false) cannot prove dependency stalls or total device time. Neither method distinguishes 128B line waste from bandwidth saturation; that distinction comes from the paired-profiling GB/s asymmetry plus the IR stride layout, so this change is predicted on load granularity while the simulator only bounds it as a load-side chain rather than a compute-side one.
unknown: Whether the Ascend backend merges the affine h,d axes into one contiguous 512B DMA run and whether BLOCK_S=32 keeps per-head 4KB stores efficient.
Whether the 4x fewer load transactions actually recover most of the 33->74 GB/s gap or whether per-core DRAM/L2 bandwidth caps the gain.
